title: Jamie Dimon Just Issued a Warning About AI Stocks. History Says the Smartest Investors Are Making This 1 Move.
excerpt: If you agree with Jamie Dimon's concerns about AI stocks, how should you invest?
content_html:
Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, is one of the most respected voices in American business. When he raises concerns about the stock market, it's worth paying attention.

In a recent interview with Wilfred Frost on the Master Investor Podcast, Dimon said that the stock market feels a little too complacent about risks. He issued a warning about the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, drawing on what happened during the dot-com boom (and bust) of the late 1990s. When asked about risks facing AI stocks, Dimon said: 

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

When I look at AI itself, the amount of money being spent is huge. Will it pay off in total? Probably, just like the internet did. Will it pay off the way you expect and the timetable you expect? Definitely not.

Dimon also mentioned that before the long-term winners of the internet stock era like Alphabet emerged, there were bankruptcies and failures among former dot-com darlings like Yahoo! and Netscape. No one knows yet which stocks will be the long-term winners of the AI trade.

So how should you invest? Based on long-term stock market history and what happened to internet stocks 25 years ago, smart investors will continue investing in broadly diversified portfolios of stocks based on fundamentals and long-term growth potential -- not short-term hype.

If you agree with Dimon's assessment that AI is likely to pay off in the long run, let's look at two exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that are worth considering today.

Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI): 3,531 stocks, 10 years of 14.5% annualized returns

If you don't know which stocks will be the big winners of AI but believe the U.S. stock market will go up in the long run, one simple move is to buy the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (NYSEMKT: VTI). This is an ultra-low-cost index fund with an expense ratio of 0.03%. It holds roughly the entire U.S. stock market in its portfolio, with a total of 3,531 stock holdings.

That includes companies of all sizes (large caps, midcaps, and small caps). This fund owns growth stocks and value stocks, tech stocks, and all kinds of other industry sectors. No matter what happens next with AI stocks, if you believe that the U.S. economy will keep growing in the long run and U.S. companies will keep generating profits, buying this total stock market ETF can be a good move for long-term investors.

摩根大通首席执行官杰米戴蒙是美国商界最受尊敬的声音之一。 当他提出对股市的担忧时，值得关注。

戴蒙最近在《投资者大师》播客上接受威尔弗雷德·弗罗斯特采访时表示，股市对风险有点过于自满了。 他借鉴 20 世纪 90 年代末互联网繁荣（和萧条）期间发生的事情，对人工智能 (AI) 繁荣发出了警告。 当被问及人工智能股票面临的风险时，戴蒙表示：

错过了 2009 年的 Nvidia？ 这个罕见的信号再次闪烁。 2009年，一家名不见经传的芯片制造商英伟达发出了“双倍下跌”的信号。 多年来，对于一家规模仅为 Nvidia 1/100 的公司来说，同样的“完全确信”信号闪烁。 继续 ”

当我审视人工智能本身时，所花费的资金是巨大的。 总共能得到回报吗？ 也许，就像互联网一样。 它会按照您期望的方式和时间表获得回报吗？ 绝对不是。

戴蒙还提到，在像Alphabet这样的互联网股票时代的长期赢家出现之前，像雅虎这样的前互联网宠儿也曾经历过破产和失败。 和网景。 目前还没有人知道哪些股票将成为人工智能交易的长期赢家。

那么应该如何投资呢？ 根据长期股市历史和 25 年前互联网股票的情况，聪明的投资者将继续根据基本面和长期增长潜力（而不是短期炒作）投资于广泛多元化的股票投资组合。

如果您同意戴蒙的评估，即从长远来看，人工智能可能会带来回报，那么让我们来看看今天值得考虑的两只交易所交易基金 (ETF)。

Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI)：3,531只股票，10年年化回报率为14.5%

如果你不知道哪些股票将成为人工智能的大赢家，但相信美国股市从长远来看会上涨，一个简单的举措就是购买先锋晨星总股票市场ETF（NYSEMKT：VTI）。 这是一只超低成本指数基金，费用率为0.03%。 它的投资组合几乎涵盖了整个美国股市，总共持有 3,531 只股票。

这包括各种规模的公司（大型股、中型股和小型股）。 该基金拥有成长股和价值股、科技股以及其他各种行业板块。 无论人工智能股票接下来会发生什么，如果你相信美国经济从长远来看将继续增长，美国公司将继续盈利，那么购买这只股票市场ETF对于长期投资者来说可能是一个不错的举措。
